fix.notes: The fix uses the existing `clauses.exclude_active_league_runs` helper that is already applied to the public deck listing for non-admins, so the logic is consistent with the rest of the codebase. The `except_person_id` parameter ensures a sorter's own active run is not hidden from them. No schema or data migration required.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The `/admin/archetypes/` sort queue (`EditArchetypes`) loaded all unreviewed decks with `WHERE NOT d.reviewed` regardless of whether the viewer was an admin or a demimod (non-admin sorter). This meant that demimod sorters could see opponents' active league runs — the deck name, cards, and person — before those runs were complete, creating an information advantage.

## What changed

In `decksite/views/edit_archetypes.py`, the deck-queue query now conditionally appends the `exclude_active_league_runs(viewer_id)` clause (already used elsewhere in the codebase via `decksite/data/clauses.py`) when the viewer does not have admin privileges. Admin users continue to see all unreviewed decks unchanged. Non-admin sorters see only decks from completed or retired league runs (plus their own active runs, which the clause exempts via `except_person_id`).

Two unit tests were added to `decksite/controllers/admin_test.py` to pin this behaviour:
- `test_edit_archetypes_excludes_active_league_runs_for_non_admin` — verifies the league-run exclusion clause is present in the `load_decks` call when no admin session key is set.
- `test_edit_archetypes_includes_active_league_runs_for_admin` — verifies that admins receive only the `NOT d.reviewed` filter (no exclusion).

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks passed)
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit decksite/controllers/admin_test.py` — 850 passed, 1 skipped (full suite run against a live MariaDB instance bootstrapped in the sandbox)

Fixes #10771
